Suspected Overdose or Toxidrome

anticholinergic · stimulant · serotonin syndrome · neuroleptic malignant syndrome · lithium · opioid and sedative · cholinergic · salicylate and acetaminophenWhich toxidrome, and what must be checked in every overdose?

1Presentation2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Presentation
Bottom line
  • Stabilize first: airway and breathing, a fingerstick glucose and an ECG (electrocardiogram); naloxone for slow breathing with pinpoint pupils
  • In every intentional overdose, check acetaminophen and salicylate levels, and suspect more than one substance
  • Then name the toxidrome from the pupils, the skin, the bowel sounds and the muscle tone
What it is

A toxidrome: a cluster of signs that points to a class of poison

Who

Intentional overdose is common in adolescents and adults, often with more than one substance

Sort by

Pupils sweating or dry skin bowel sounds tone and reflexes

Timing: minutes to hours, or days, after a drug is started or raised

Treatment in

2Urgent risks
BreathingSlow, shallow breathing with pinpoint pupils

If breathing is slow or the airway is at risk, choose assisted ventilation and IV naloxone.

GlucoseAltered consciousness or a depressed nervous system

If a bedside glucose has not ruled out hypoglycemia, choose IV dextrose, with thiamine given with or before it in alcohol use or undernutrition.

HeartA wide QRS, ventricular arrhythmia or hypotension

If the QRS is over 100 ms after a tricyclic, choose sodium bicarbonate.

Another causeInfection, head injury, hypoglycemia, stroke or Wernicke encephalopathy can also alter consciousness

If the toxidrome does not fit the picture, choose look for another cause of altered consciousness.

Suicide attemptAny intentional ingestion

If the patient is medically stable and thinking clearly, choose assess suicide risk.

3Differential
Which toxidrome, most tempting first
ToxidromeFingerprintDecides it
Big pupils; hot, dry, flushed skin; ileus; urinary retention; delirium Anticholinergic toxidromeHot as a hare (fever), dry as a bone (no sweating), red as a beet (flushing), blind as a bat (big pupils), mad as a hatter (delirium)Dry skin with normal tone; a tricyclic may add a wide QRS
Big pupils, fast pulse, hypertension, agitation, fever, seizuresSweating, with the same big pupils and fever
Clonus, hyperreflexia, sweating, ↑ bowel soundsMinutes to hours after a serotonergic drug is added or raised; clonus
Fever, lead-pipe rigidity, confusion, unstable vital signsBuilds over 1 to 3 days after a dopamine blocker is started or raised; rigid, with slow reflexes
Acute: vomiting and diarrhea first. Chronic: coarse tremor, ataxia, seizuresUsually within 10 days of adding a thiazide; an NSAID (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug) or an ACE (angiotensin-converting enzyme) inhibitor also raises the level
Pinpoint pupils, slow breathing, sedationPupils under 1 mm with slow breathing
Sedation with normal-sized pupilsBreathing only mildly slowed; abnormal vital signs suggest alcohol taken as well
Cholinergic (organophosphate)Pinpoint pupils, sweating, salivation, tearing, diarrhea, bronchospasm, bradycardiaWet: secretions everywhere, with ↑ bowel sounds
Salicylate (aspirin)Fever, tinnitus, fast breathingRespiratory alkalosis early, metabolic acidosis late; a salicylate level confirms
AcetaminophenOften no symptoms earlyLiver failure may follow 1 to a few days later
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
SSRI (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) overdose with confusion or an abnormal examA coingestant: an SSRI alone is usually well toleratedLevels of common coingestants, such as salicylate and ethanol
Agitated, hallucinating and febrile on clozapine or a tricyclicAnticholinergic toxicity; haloperidol would worsen itA benzodiazepine
Normal muscle tone in that patientNot neuroleptic malignant syndromeNo bromocriptine; ECG
Farmer with pinpoint pupils, tearing, vomiting and ↑ bowel soundsOrganophosphate poisoningAtropine first, then pralidoxime
Pinpoint pupils, slow breathing, sedationOpioid toxicityIV naloxone; intubation if no quick response
Lithium with vomiting and diarrhea, then tremor and ataxiaLithium toxicityLithium level
Acetaminophen taken, no symptoms yetDelayed liver injuryN-acetylcysteine; activated charcoal within 4 hours

Pause point. The bait: haloperidol for an agitated, febrile patient on psychiatric drugs, or a negative urine screen read as no poisoning. Screens miss many drugs; name the toxidrome from the exam and check the acetaminophen level anyway.

Practice
  1. 28-year-old woman on fluoxetine, started tramadol for back pain yesterday agitated, sweating, shivering; clonus at both ankles reflexes brisk; bowel sounds hyperactive; pupils 6 mm T 38.4 °C · HR 122/min → Serotonin syndrome → within a day of adding tramadol to an SSRI, clonus, hyperreflexia, sweating and active bowel sounds mean serotonin syndrome; neuroleptic malignant syndrome brings lead-pipe rigidity over days on a dopamine blocker, and anticholinergic skin is dry
  2. 17-year-old girl took a handful of her mother's pills 2 hours ago alert, oriented; says she wanted to die pupils, skin and bowel sounds normal ECG normal · glucose 96 mg/dL · urine screen negative → Serum acetaminophen level → an intentional ingestion needs an acetaminophen level even when the exam is normal, because early acetaminophen poisoning is often silent and the antidote prevents delayed liver injury; suicide risk is assessed once she is medically clear
  3. 33-year-old man found unresponsive in a public restroom by a friend pupils pinpoint; shallow, slow breaths; groans to a sternal rub needle marks on both forearms; no head injury seen RR 6/min · SpO2 84% · glucose 110 mg/dL → Intravenous naloxone → pinpoint pupils with slow breathing mean opioid toxicity: assisted ventilation and naloxone first, with intubation only if there is no quick response; a benzodiazepine overdose leaves the pupils normal
  4. 46-year-old farmer brought in an hour after spraying his crops vomiting, drooling, tearing; wheezing on both sides pupils 1 mm; bowel sounds hyperactive; diffuse sweating; muscle twitching HR 48/min · BP 98/60 mm Hg → Organophosphate poisoning → pinpoint pupils with secretions everywhere, wheezing and bradycardia after crop spraying mean cholinergic poisoning from an organophosphate; an opioid leaves the patient dry, and anticholinergic toxicity has big pupils and dry skin
  5. 38-year-old woman took an unknown number of pills after an argument ringing in both ears; nausea, vomiting breathing fast and deep; mildly confused T 38.3 °C · RR 30/min · pupils 4 mm → Salicylate poisoning → fever, tinnitus and fast breathing after an overdose point to aspirin, with respiratory alkalosis early and metabolic acidosis later; a salicylate level confirms it
  6. 22-year-old man swallowed 30 sertraline tablets 3 hours ago drowsy, confused; answers slowly no clonus; reflexes normal; pupils 5 mm HR 104/min · BP 118/76 mm Hg · ECG: QRS 92 ms → Levels of common coingestants → an SSRI overdose alone is usually well tolerated, so confusion means another substance: check coingestant levels such as salicylate and ethanol; cyproheptadine is for refractory serotonin syndrome, which this is not
Pairs with Anticholinergic and Tricyclic Toxicity: QRS width, bicarbonate, no physostigmine with a tricyclic. SSRI Adverse Effects: serotonin syndrome. Antipsychotic Adverse Effects: neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Lithium Therapy: toxicity and dialysis. Substance Intoxication and Withdrawal: illicit drugs and alcohol.
Transferable rule

In a suspected overdose, stabilize breathing, glucose and the heart, check acetaminophen and salicylate levels, then let the pupils, skin, bowel sounds and tone name the toxidrome.
